newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE approves 1997 budget, spending of $5.41 bln.
newsitem.headline: UAE approves 1997 budget, spending of $5.41 bln.

text.p: The oil-rich United Arab Emirates on Monday approved its 1997 federal budget, raising spending to 19.86 billion dirhams ($5.41 billion) with a projected deficit of 987 million dirhams.
The spending figure climbed from last year's 18.25 billion dirhams. Revenue was forecast at 18.87 billion dirhams, up from 17.40 billion in 1996.
The budget was approved by the cabinet, the official WAM news agency said.
WAM did not say what oil prices the budget was based on. But the UAE, like other Gulf Arab states, has been showered with extra petrodollars due to stronger oil prices in the past few months.
The agency did not give a detailed breakdown of the budget.
The UAE, with an Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries supply quota of 2.161 million barrels per day, derives about 75 percent of government revenue from oil.
The UAE, one of the few oil producers with spare production capacity and sufficient reserves of crude to last a century, has an estimated annual oil income of $9 billion.
Bankers estimate the country's federal budget represents only one third of real consolidated spending of the seven emirates that make up the federation.
The vast bulk of the spending is pumped into education, health and other services as well as salaries for civil servants.
Most of the federal budget is shouldered by Abu Dhabi, the wealthiest of the emirates with an estimated per capita income of $29,000.
